notes: Requesty ~22k-decision benchmark run 2026-10-05 through its production router (one run, one day, one client location). Requesty SELLS these models, so it is not neutral about them; the doc is independent of the model vendors. Values are read from labelled bars in the post charts (23 PNGs; chart 01-23 named per row) plus article text, so they are as precise as the printed labels. Open benchmark: 2,000 typed decisions + Banking77 + AG News + Emotion + a 1,000-item MASSIVE subset, one question per call. Gateway benchmark: 2,000 items over six tasks; routing labels are Claude Opus 5.5 labels (agreement with Opus, not truth). Latency is client wall-clock INCLUDING the router hop (4-8 in flight): the same Clef weights are 200 ms apart depending on who serves them. cloudflare/clef hit Cloudflare daily Workers AI quota mid-run: full coverage only on typed decisions, Banking77 and Emotion; 62 AG News items; no MASSIVE. The charts label Jev numbers "TypeSafe Jev 1.13 (published)": they equal the morrenhale dataset (see that doc) and were NOT run by Requesty, so they are not duplicated here. LLM baselines resolve to model-catalog ids; accuracy for LLMs counts only items they answered.

claims.statement: Requesty (Oct 5): decision models returned 0 unusable answers in 2,000 items each; "GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6 Luna and GPT-5 Nano on Azure could not answer 33% to 36% of the toxic-chat prompts" (content filter or refusal); Opus 5.5 hit content_filter on 14 items.
claims.implication: For moderation steps, no-refusal is a genuine operational advantage of decision models over content-filtered LLMs.

claims.statement: Requesty (gateway benchmark, human-labeled fields): Clef averages 83.2%, "3.4 points below Claude Opus 5.5, at 3% of Opus's cost and a quarter of its latency"; the Perplexity decider 81.8% at $0.02 per 1,000 items. Decision models are weakest on multi-level scores: tool-call gating 68.7% (Clef and Perplexity) vs Opus 90.0% and GPT-5.5 85.7%; 3-level complexity agreement with Opus 51.9% (Clef), 56.1% (Perplexity), 81.7% (GPT-5.5).

Requesty: binary noul questions are about 10 points more accurate than ordered score rubrics (noul 79-82% vs score/choice 69-72% on the typed set; "a stack of binary noul questions is more reliable than one multi-level score").
claims.implication: Prefer noul questions to score questions where the decision allows it.

claims.statement: Requesty confidence-coverage curve (1,600 human-labeled decisions): keeping the 80% of decisions Clef is most confident about gives 82% accuracy, the top half 86%; the Perplexity decider 80% at 80% coverage and 88% at 50%. Thresholds must be fitted per provider (the confidence field is not portable).
claims.implication: Confidence-gated escalation works but fit thresholds on your own traffic and per provider.

claims.statement: Requesty request caps: "Sference caps a request at 16 questions, Cloudflare at 64, Perplexity at 128." Confidence field: "Sference returns the maximum probability. Cloudflare returns something else, consistently lower. Perplexity returns a third thing that equals the max probability on a quarter of items".
